provenance.cardiac_output: this project's cardiac model (four-chamber time-varying elastance + Windkessel, 60.5 s resting window)
provenance.renal_fraction: textbook magnitude (the kidneys receive about 20-25 % of cardiac output); NOT measured in this project

single_nephron.nephron_count_source: published order of magnitude (~1e6 per kidney); NOT measured here
single_nephron.derivation: SNBF = RBF / nephron count; SNGFR = GFR / nephron count; efferent blood flow = SNBF - SNGFR (the filtered plasma has left the capillary). No coefficient is fitted anywhere in this chain.

emergent_result.why: about a fifth of the plasma entering the glomerulus is filtered off, so LESS blood leaves than enters — yet it leaves FASTER, because the efferent arteriole is the narrower vessel. Both numbers fall out of the published calibres and the model's own GFR; neither was fitted.

pulsatility.waveform: this project's cardiac model, mean aortic pressure beat over 40 beats
pulsatility.limitation: the coupling is purely resistive — no inertance, no arterial compliance — so the modelled pulse is flatter than a real renal Doppler trace and the resistive index comes out below the published 0.5-0.7. The peak systolic velocities reported per level inherit that under-prediction. No gain has been applied to hide it.

audit.direction_check: arterial and glomerular paths are stored hilum -> terminal, venous paths terminal -> caval ostium, urine papilla -> bladder. Each path is traversed in one direction only and the renderer advances phase monotonically, so no path can produce a retrograde sample.

mass_balance_mL_min.note: venous return is set equal to arterial inflow. The filtered load that leaves as urine (1.5 mL/min of 1139) is 0.13 % and is carried by the collecting system, not subtracted from the venous return.

audit.urine_transport_caveat: real ureteric urine transport is PERISTALTIC — boluses propelled by 2-6 contractions per minute, not steady flow. What is computed here is the steady-flow equivalent velocity of the same volume rate, shown at a declared display gain so its direction is visible at all.
